assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks (magic-wavelength trapping proposed by Katori, then realised with Sr and developed by Ye to uncertainties near 1e-18) are a clean, concrete step in what we can measure and how accurately. The leap beyond microwave Cs standards enables relativistic geodesy, tests of fundamental constants and a redefinition of the second. The idea is original, the physics is clear and the technique is already a global tool.
assessment.attribution: Katori made the decisive magic-wavelength proposal and first lattice-clock demonstration; Ye drove the many-body, Sr-lattice precision frontier and frequency-comb connection. The credited pair maps well onto the discovery. Others (e.g. Hall and Hänsch for combs, Wineland for ion clocks) were already honoured, and the two names are cleanly separable from those.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation across several laboratories (JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, NIST, PTB, SYRTE and others) is strong, and agreement between clocks at the 1e-18 level is documented. Timing is mature: the redefinition of the second is under discussion and the field is stable.
uncertainties: Ion-clock contributions (Al+ and others) may be argued to be an overlapping branch of optical clock recognition.
Whether the committee wishes to split credit with optical-frequency-comb or ion-clock work is not settled by the supplied text.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Coherent interfaces between light and matter (cavity QED single-atom photon control, EIT-based storage and slow light, quantum state transfer, atom-photon entanglement) are the foundation for quantum memories, repeaters and quantum networks. This is a field I know closely from rare-earth and atomic-ensemble memories; the lasting impact on quantum technology is large and the underlying concepts are original and clear.
assessment.attribution: Rempe (single-atom cavity QED networks, state transfer), Kimble (quantum network vision, DLCZ-type protocols, cavity QED) and Lukin (EIT storage and light-matter protocols) are central. The candidate bundles several platforms; rare-earth-crystal, Raman and ensemble memories contribute but are not credited here, so the allocation is not unique. I note my own field proximity and treat that cautiously.
assessment.maturity: Experimental confirmation is extensive across platforms, and elementary networks have been demonstrated. Full scalable networks remain developing, but the basic light-matter interface is mature enough for recognition.
uncertainties: The compound nature of the topic means different platforms (single atoms, ensembles, solid-state memories) could need distinct recognition.
Conceptual priority between ensemble-memory protocols from several groups is not fully resolved by the text supplied.
My own research proximity may bias the assessment; I cannot independently verify priority claims.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom interferometry turned matter-wave coherence into a precision sensor for gravity, rotation, the fine-structure constant and tests of equivalence principles. It directly embodies measurement-limited progress and has spawned practical gravimeters and gradiometers. The concept is original and the sensitivity impact is lasting.
assessment.attribution: Bordé's early theoretical and Ramsey-Bordé interferometry work, Pritchard's atom-optics and interferometer demonstrations and Kasevich's inertial-sensing realisations are decisive. Müller and others are credited too but follow later precision refinements. Chu (Nobel 1997 for cooling) and Ramsey-type methods complicate the boundary. Three names give a defensible configuration, though ordering of priority among Pritchard, Mlynek, Kasevich and Chu is arguable.
assessment.maturity: Matter-wave interferometers are repeatedly confirmed in many laboratories and applications are emerging. Fundamental-physics results (large-scale gradient measurements, G, alpha) are still evolving, but the core technique is stable.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 1997 and 2001 AMO prizes may reduce perceived novelty.
Credit among the several 1991 groups (Pritchard, Mlynek, Kasevich-Chu) cannot be resolved from the supplied names alone.
Whether Müller should replace Bordé depends on emphasis between early theory and precision application.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental discovery of the Higgs boson at the LHC completed the Standard Model and is arguably the central experimental result of 21st century particle physics. Importance, clarity and confirmation are exceptional. As an atomic physicist I defer on detector details but the impact is plain.
assessment.attribution: The 2013 prize recognised theorists only. The experimental discovery was by thousands of collaborators; a one-to-three configuration necessarily singles out leadership figures. Jenni and Virdee (and Della Negra) as founders and Gianotti as ATLAS spokesperson at discovery are the usual candidates, but this is a hard and partly unfair allocation under the three-person rule, and alternatives exist.
assessment.maturity: Fully confirmed by both experiments, with properties measured since 2012; recognition is not premature, though the experimental part is arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Fair selection of at most three laureates among ATLAS and CMS leaders is genuinely contested; Della Negra is a plausible substitute.
Possible perception that the 2013 prize already settled the discovery.
I cannot verify internal collaboration roles from the supplied material.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect opened a new class of quantum matter classified by topology, with spin-momentum-locked edge and surface states. The theoretical prediction followed by experimental realisation is a classic Nobel pattern and the concept is highly original and influential.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the foundational prediction; Molenkamp's group experimentally demonstrated the HgTe quantum spin Hall state following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal and Konig et al. Hasan (3D topological insulators) is an alternative, and Bernevig, Zhang and Fu are not on this credited list, which limits the fairness of any configuration.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmations across HgTe, Bi-based materials and ARPES are well established. The 2016 prize recognised topological phases generally, which creates overlap, but this specific discovery has remained stable.
uncertainties: The 2016 Nobel Prize in Physics on topological phase transitions may be seen as having covered part of this ground.
Absent from the supplied names: contributions by Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang and Fu may be decisive.
Choice between Molenkamp and Hasan is a judgement call.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Theoretical prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the subsequent discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created the moire-materials field, with tunable quantum matter at the heart of current condensed-matter research. The idea is original and impact has been rapid and large.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald provided the continuum theory of the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the decisive experiments. Cao, Fatemi and others on the experimental team, and Efetov and Dean, are not on the credited list, which leaves a question about whether the experimental credit is correctly concentrated.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many groups with extensive follow-up, though the microscopic origin of superconductivity remains under debate. Recognition is probably slightly early but plausible.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism and reproducibility of device-dependent features are not fully settled.
Credit for student and postdoc contributions and for other moire pioneers is uncertain.
Possible prematurity relative to a decade-scale maturation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation of the Hubbard model with ultracold atoms in optical lattices, including superfluid to Mott insulator transition, fermionic Hubbard physics and single-site quantum gas microscopy, provides controlled access to many-body quantum problems. I value the experimental control and the link to precision atomic-physics techniques. Impact is lasting and conceptually clear.
assessment.attribution: Theory (Jaksch, Zoller, Cirac) and experiment (Greiner, Bloch, Esslinger and others) are both important; the credited list has five names, so one to three experiments-first names is a pragmatic choice. Cirac and Zoller are better placed under B025, so I keep this entry experimental. Kasevich/Hänsch/Cornell-Wieman prizes previously honoured the BEC foundation.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently confirmed by numerous groups; quantum-gas microscopes, fermionic Mott insulators and antiferromagnetic correlations are well reproduced. Usefulness for solving open problems (e.g. d-wave phases) is still developing.
uncertainties: Whether simulation results have yet answered an open scientific question is debated.
Division between theoretical proposal credit and experimental credit is not settled.
Overlap with the AMO prizes of 2001 and 2012.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical addressing, coherent control and readout of single defect spins in diamond (NV centres) launched solid-state quantum sensing and elementary quantum networks, including room-temperature magnetometry and loophole-free Bell tests with remote spins. The technique is original and broadly useful, from nanoscale NMR to biology, aligned with the importance of measurement capability.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup (first optical detection of single NV spins), Awschalom (spin control and defect qubits) and Hanson (entanglement and networks) are major; Lukin and Walsworth contribute sensing and protocol innovations and a five-person credit list shows no single clean division. The proposed three leave out important contributors.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in many laboratories with commercial instrument development; the quantum-network side is younger. Recognition is plausible but could be considered slightly early for networks, mature for sensing.
uncertainties: Compound discovery: sensing and networking contributions may require different recognition.
Credit split among five credited names is unresolved.
Whether the application results are considered fundamental enough for the physics prize.
